headline: Reuters reported Oct 1, citing Marisks, that three oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles in Hormuz on Sep 29. Iran received a US response to its proposal, but sequencing disagreements remain and no reopening agreement is verified. Reuters Sep 28 documents selective Qatar-linked LNG passages, without a complete weekly transit count. Reuters reported Oct 1 that Chinese refiners suspended fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, citing four sources; December Brent settled at $102.31 (+4.37%).

evidence.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?
evidence.note: Al Jazeera reported Kpler data showing Hormuz daily vessel transits ranging from 5 to 11 this week against a 10-day average of about 13, still well below pre-crisis norms.

evidence.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?
evidence.note: Al Jazeera reported the US and Iran fought a direct tanker war Sep 5-6: CENTCOM struck three Iranian oil tankers while Iran fired missiles at a US carrier and destroyer and hit three tankers plus three US-linked vessels.

evidence.title: GME Exchange Products Daily Information Bulletin - Sep 25, 2026

evidence.title: Iran-Gulf talks shelved as Oman says conditions not right
evidence.note: Re-scraped The National's Sep 14 article. It records Oman's postponement of the proposed Iran-Gulf meeting; its traffic figures remain dated historical context.

evidence.title: Oil tanker rates hit record highs following Iran, US shipping attacks
evidence.note: Re-scraped the exact Reuters Sep 11 article. The latest reviewed same-unit Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC observation remains Worldscale 450, approximately $11.50/bbl.

evidence.title: Oil settles up around 4% as Iran's president vows to never surrender
evidence.note: Reuters reported Sep 23 that Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, while indirect US-Iran talks discussed reopening Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade. Iran's position on reopening remained conditional.

evidence.title: US-Iran conflict helps drive wave of supertanker orders
evidence.note: Reuters reported Sep 17 that Strait of Hormuz tanker crossings remain in single digits (LSEG data) as shipowners order a record wave of VLCCs to serve longer Atlantic-to-Asia routes.

evidence.title: Crude oil exports via Hormuz at 33.7 million barrels this week, data shows
evidence.note: Re-scraped the exact Reuters Sep 25 article. Kpler reported nine commodity-vessel transits on Sep 24, 33.7 million barrels of crude exports week-to-date, and 19 tankers including 17 VLCCs.

evidence.title: Oil slides as US-Iran truce hopes outweigh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
evidence.note: Reuters reported Brent settled at 104.32 USD/bbl on Sep 25, down 2.1%, as truce hopes outweighed attack risk. The article also reported Brent at 105.11 at 05:41 GMT, six Houthi missiles intercepted near Taif/Yanbu, and no resumption of Yanbu tanker loadings.

evidence.title: Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship oil transfers reach limit as Saudi exports surge
evidence.note: Reuters reported September Saudi crude exports via Hormuz on track for 3.6 million bpd, while Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship operations reached capacity. A $1.27 million/day Middle East-to-China VLCC time-charter quote was reported for Sep 21.

evidence.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions linger as Iran and US move further from a deal
evidence.note: Al Jazeera reported Sep 27 that Tehran instructed shipping companies to use a temporary Iran-approved Hormuz route and pay fees; full reopening remains conditional on ending the US blockade. Reports of explosions were attributed to Iranian media and were not confirmed by Iranian authorities.

evidence.title: Mideast oil exports rebound in September as Saudi Arabia boosts shipments
evidence.note: Re-reviewed Sep 30: Reuters updated Sep 28 preliminary Kpler estimates to regional exports 16.328 million bpd, Hormuz 9.719 million bpd, and Ras Tanura 3.25 million bpd.

evidence.note: Qatar said it was exchanging messages between the US and Iran to establish common ground. Trump denied offering sanctions relief or release of frozen funds; negotiations had not produced a Hormuz reopening agreement.

evidence.title: Oil prices settle down 2.5% on signs Middle East exports recovering
evidence.note: Reuters reported Saudi Arabia resumed Yanbu tanker loadings after restarting East-West Pipeline operations. Reuters reported Sep 29 Brent settlement at $102.59/bbl and WTI at $89.38/bbl; these are separate settlement observations from Yahoo snapshots.

evidence.title: Three oil tankers hit by projectiles in Hormuz strait on Tuesday, Marisks says
evidence.note: Marisks reported three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting Hormuz on Sep 29. Reuters names Al Ruwais, Mersin Prosperity and Sinbad; Marisks said AIS transponders were off.

evidence.title: Iran says it receives US response to latest proposal
evidence.note: Iran said it received a US response to its latest proposal. An official briefed on the talks said the parties disagree about the sequence of steps; no reopening agreement was reported.

evidence.title: Qatar-linked LNG traffic through Hormuz strait picks up despite conflict
evidence.note: Reuters/LSEG/Kpler tracked GasLog Skagen off Sri Lanka Sep 27 with a Ras Laffan cargo. Al Shamal reappeared outside Hormuz around Sep 24-25; Al Ghashamiya delivered to Dahej Sep 24. The report describes individual sightings and dark AIS transits, not a complete comparable weekly LNG count.

evidence.title: Oil jumps 4% on reports China halts fuel exports, US troops head to Middle East
evidence.note: Reuters reports Chinese refiners suspended oil-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, citing four sources. The new front-month December Brent contract settled at $102.31, +4.37%; WTI settled at $92.87, +2.71%, on Oct 1. Reuters cites a Wall Street Journal report that the US is sending a third aircraft carrier and up to 10,000 additional troops; these deployments are reported plans.

observations.label: Edison: QatarEnergy extends force majeure
observations.value: Reuters reported that QatarEnergy renewed force-majeure notices through November after Iranian strikes damaged two of 14 Ras Laffan LNG trains; it is seeking 2-3 MTPA of US LNG through 2031
